name: בַּעַל
summary: Above all the god of Canaan, הַבַּעַל “the lord”, whom Israel served in the days of the judges and under Ahab and Manasseh, and the Baal of Peor to whom Israel joined itself in Moab (Num 25:3; Psa 106:28). The noun בַּעַל is an owner, husband or lord, and the god's name is that title. Two men also bore it: a Reubenite, the son of Reaiah (1Ch 5:5), and a Benjamite of Gibeon, son of Jeiel, uncle of Kish (1Ch 8:30; 9:36), in the days when the word could still be said of Yahweh (Hos 2:18).

evidence.note: “They forsook Yahweh and served the Baal and the Ashtaroth.”
“If Yahweh is the God, go after him; but if the Baal, go after him.”
“Israel joined himself to Baal of Peor (בַעַל פְּעוֹר), and the anger of Yahweh burned.”
“All the men who went after Baal of Peor, Yahweh your God destroyed.”
“They joined themselves to Baal of Peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.”
“They came to Baal of Peor and consecrated themselves to the shame.”
“Who have not bowed the knee to Baal (Βάαλ)”, from 1Ki 19:18.
“Reaiah his son, בַּעַל his son”, of Reuben.
“His firstborn son Abdon, then Zur, Kish, בַּעַל and Nadab”: the sons of Jeiel at Gibeon.
“You shall call me my man, and shall no longer call me my Baal (בַּעְלִי).”

note: TIPNR's Supernatural record Baal@Num.25.3 takes בַּעַל and בַּעַל פְּעוֹר. No bdb key: the god's tokens and the two men's are in b.ci.ab and b.ci.ac with the noun, which the root entry's noun holds, and a key belongs to one entry only; Baal-peor (b.ci.aj) has as its tokens פְּעוֹר, filed by spelling. Ugaritic and Phoenician are named because there too the god's name is the epithet “lord, owner”.
